Evidence transparency: Ratings are reported as published by their original sources and are not independently reassessed by this site. We identify the source and publication date, note when ratings are outdated or guidelines differ, and distinguish profile completeness from the strength of the supporting evidence.

Use the diagnosis filter for broad diagnostic families. Search prioritizes treatment names, conditions, goals, and potential fit; if no direct matches are found, it searches profile details and evidence notes.

0 selected

Choose two or three profiles to compare.

How this site is built: It reorganizes ratings and recommendations published by the Society of Clinical Psychology, the APA, and Psychotherapies at a Glance. AI tools helped draft summaries, but AI does not approve interventions, assign ratings, or decide what is recommended. A missing rating or profile never means a treatment is ineffective, and a treatment’s popularity is not evidence for it. This is not individualized treatment advice.
Testing this version? Tasks and how to send feedback
  1. Search for a client concern you see often. Can you find a relevant treatment within a minute?
  2. Open two profiles and use Compare. Is it clear what each source says and what it does not?
  3. Open one source link. Does it match what the profile says?
  4. Check one training note. Does it match what you know about that treatment?

Send comments, errors and missing treatments to lalocarn@umich.edu. Include the treatment name and what you expected. Training notes are category-level prompts that a clinician has not yet reviewed.

How to read the results: Evidence strength and clinical fit are separate questions. Findings for one diagnosis, population, protocol, or outcome should not automatically be generalized to another. Always inspect the original research and use clinical judgment.
About this source index: This index is restricted to the Society of Clinical Psychology current and archived treatment lists, APA clinical practice guidelines, and Psychotherapies at a Glance. It is a work in progress, not a complete list of every treatment in those sources. Ratings are shown as the original source reports them; organizations may use different criteria, so ratings should not be compared as if they mean exactly the same thing. A missing rating does not mean a treatment lacks evidence.
How to use this index: It is a discovery layer. Ratings are copied as shown on each source, not re-graded. The status "Listed by source · rating as published · not reviewed by this site" means we have not yet extracted study-level evidence for that entry. Treatments with a full profile open our evidence record.
Source coverage audit · updated October 19, 2026: This page tracks which treatments from the selected sources have been added to the site and which still need checking. It does not confirm that every source has been fully captured. Ratings keep the original source's wording and date; we do not create our own ratings. Profile status shows how much information has been added to this site, not how strong the evidence is. When a rating is missing or sources differ, that uncertainty is kept visible. “Scope review” means we need to decide whether an item belongs in this psychotherapy-focused resource.
How matches are handled: Each source entry keeps its original identifier where available. When an entry is matched to a treatment profile, the match method is recorded. Entries with uncertain matches remain flagged for review, and a source link alone does not mean the treatment has been fully appraised.

Release-readiness snapshot

Automated structural checks only. These counts help prioritize review; they do not establish clinical accuracy or readiness for patient care.

Functional smoke-test report

These checks verify that expected controls and core functions are present in the current page. They do not simulate real browser clicks, validate downloaded files, or replace manual cross-browser testing.

  1. Run the tests to check key page controls and functions.

Required before a clinician pilot

Performance note: repeated source-duplicate checks are cached during the audit so large source sets can render without rescanning the entire library for every row.

  • Review high-priority source mismatches and unresolved profile links.
  • Verify source wording, population, intervention components, dose, caveats, and training requirements against the original documents.
  • Manually test search, diagnosis filters, profile details, comparison behavior, source links, and CSV exports in a browser.
  • Have a qualified clinical reviewer check safety language, medication-related content, and scope boundaries.
  • Run a small usability pilot and record issues before public release.

Source-to-profile match integrity

Automated checks look for missing links, generated source-only summaries, invalid source URLs, and possible diagnosis-domain mismatches. These are triage signals, not definitive judgments; a human must confirm the match against the original source and target population. Cross-source name matches are counted for comparison and do not mean the ratings should be merged. Source records are linked to a detailed profile only when the intervention family and population are sufficiently aligned; broad or historical source labels may remain source-only rather than being forced onto a narrower protocol.

Review progress is stored locally on this device.

Use the “Match / integrity check” filter above to work through potential mismatches, source-link problems, generated summaries, possible within-source duplicates, or strong-rated/guideline records in batches. The source-audit CSV includes blank manual-verification columns for tracking source, match, rating, population, protocol/dose, caveats/training, reviewer, date, and notes. Each source row also has an in-browser review tracker for stage, reviewer, and notes; export the CSV to preserve or share that work because browser-local status does not travel with the HTML file. Duplicate flags are prompts to compare records, not instructions to merge them.

Clinical profile quality-control audit

Automated completeness checks now assess 13 dimensions, including source metadata, HTTPS links, transparency of source-only status, and mention of outcome monitoring. The full verification matrix exports every check per profile. A populated field is not proof that its clinical content is accurate; verify against the linked source and intervention manual. Guideline recommendations should be checked against the issuing organization’s current version and update status; original ratings and their framework are preserved rather than silently regraded.

Live-source coverage check · October 18, 2026
  • Society of Clinical Psychology current list: the live page currently links to 5 current treatment entries; the index has 5 current-list records.
  • SCP archived list: the live page reports 84 archived entries; this index now contains 84 archive records after checking the paginated source pages and adding the eight previously missing entries (GAD; CBT for bulimia; CBT for anorexia; CBT for adult ADHD; CBT for chronic headache; psychoeducation for bipolar disorder; supported employment; EMDR). Archived ratings are historical, not current reappraisals, and EMDR is explicitly marked “update pending” on the archive page.
  • APA clinical practice guidelines: the live page lists guideline areas for depression, childhood/adolescent obesity, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and adult PTSD. PTSD intervention records have now been updated to reflect the 2025 guideline: CBT, CPT, and PE are strongly recommended; cognitive therapy, EMDR, NET, and four medications receive conditional recommendations. The depression guideline now includes age-specific adolescent and older-adult psychotherapy entries; the obesity guideline includes the family-based multicomponent recommendation. The depression entries have been checked against APA’s current guideline page and age-cohort treatment pages. Chronic-pain rows have been reconciled to APA’s published guideline summary by recommendation category and named pain site/comparator; the table below lists the guideline PDF’s recommendations and cross-checks them against APA’s downloadable grid; two workbook-only rows (massage and yoga for chronic low back pain) were checked against the published PDF and do not appear there as suggested recommendations.
  • Psychotherapies at a Glance: the index captures the 13 broad modalities and Table 2 disorder mappings, plus five named derivatives/adaptations identified in the article text. The online supplement (a 3-page table of at-a-glance descriptions) was supplied and read on October 18, 2026. It describes the same 13 modalities as Table 1, plus five named adaptations (BA, ERP, MBCT, ACT and IPSRT), with disorder indications, format, dose and rationale. It adds no further interventions beyond those, and its disorder mappings match the index. Format and dose are now recorded in the notes.
APA chronic pain guideline · recommendation-by-recommendation reconciliation (October 18, 2026)

These 41 rows start from APA’s published 2024 guideline PDF (guideline PDF ↗), with intervention, pain site, comparator, outcome horizon and tier kept as separate fields. The PDF extraction was machine-assisted and condensed, so confirm each row against the PDF. Each row was then checked against APA’s recommendation grid (XLSX) ↗, which has 56 comparison columns. The workbook appears to be the panel’s working grid (it contains template prompts and draft wording), so it may not match the final guideline exactly. Two rows (massage and yoga for chronic low back pain) are “suggested” in the workbook but not in the published PDF, which was re-checked on October 18, 2026: it lists massage only as insufficient evidence, and yoga only inside the “exercise over yoga” recommendation. They are shown as workbook-draft-only rows, and the published PDF should be treated as the authoritative version. Tier and comparator go together: for example, spinal manipulation is “suggested” against usual care or attention control but has insufficient evidence against exercise. “Insufficient evidence” does not mean an intervention is ineffective.

Source scope and audit status

The current index includes Society of Clinical Psychology current criteria and archived Chambless–Hollon ratings, APA clinical practice guidelines, Psychotherapies at a Glance, and separately labeled book mentions that are not evidence ratings. This pass does not add treatments or source records. Remaining work is corrective: verify existing source-to-profile links and population fit, remove entries outside psychotherapy scope, preserve original source ratings and recommendation wording, and test the interface. Archived SCP ratings remain historical and are not interchangeable with current Tolin-criteria ratings; absence from the SCP list does not establish that a treatment lacks evidence. Source inclusion alone does not prove that every profile detail is supported by the linked record.

Source-index metadata and provenance snapshot · October 19, 2026

This index includes Society of Clinical Psychology current criteria and archived Chambless–Hollon ratings, APA clinical practice guidelines, Psychotherapies at a Glance, and separately labeled book mentions that are not evidence ratings. Structural inclusion does not prove that a URL is live or that a linked source supports every detail in a profile; treatment-specific recommendation matching remains a separate task.

Source-index scope and overlap: The live index retains source records from the approved evidence sources plus separately labeled book mentions; the live catalogue retains only profiles linked to those records. Unapproved records and unlinked profiles are excluded from this version; retained source ratings are not re-graded. Shared URLs indicate a common source document, not independent corroborating studies. Historical audit statistics from earlier versions should not be interpreted as counts for the current filtered index. Audit rule: source ratings and recommendation wording remain attributable to the original source; the site does not independently re-grade studies. A source rating is not a guarantee of individual benefit or confirmation that a treatment is appropriate for a specific client.
